summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: Block envisions bitcoin for all
articles.description: The company’s head of bitcoin, Miles Suter, has two big tasks: Make bitcoin a routine payment tool and change the global financial system.

articles.title: How agentic payments present risk
articles.description: “There's no clear legal rule for who bears the loss when an AI tool exceeds its mandate,” writes one financial services consultant. “That's a problem for issuers as they contemplate making credentials available to AI tools.”

articles.title: Amex dinged by Fed, OCC
articles.description: American Express must pay a $350 million penalty after regulators cited “significant deficiencies” in its anti-money laundering program.

articles.title: Treasury taps data to fend off fraud
articles.description: The U.S. department has increased its scrutiny of payments using new sources of data in an attempt to stem past ‘pay and chase’ patterns.

articles.title: Finance leaders fight deepfakes
articles.description: Corporate finance departments are grappling with AI-enabled fraud, according to the results of a new survey by Early Warning Services’ Certos.

articles.title: Amex advises businesses on AI
articles.description: As consumers start using artificial intelligence to comparison shop, American Express aims to guide merchants in using the new technology.

articles.title: Payments income bolsters banks
articles.description: Income from card, digital and other rails has swelled to about 40% of revenue for the global bank industry, according to consulting firm McKinsey.

articles.title: SAP expands into payments
articles.description: A new service from the software firm supports multiple payment methods, including wires and stablecoin-based transactions, the company said.
